messages.content: Tell me some of the major airports in the United States.

message.content:
Here’s an overview of several of the largest and most significant commercial airports across the United States—ranked roughly by passenger traffic (pre‑COVID) and noted for their size, connectivity, and economic impact: | Airport | City / State | IATA Code | Key Highlights | |---------|--------------|-----------|----------------| | **Hartsfield–Jackson Atlanta International** | Atlanta, GA | ATL | • Largest U.S. airport by enplanements (~110 M passengers).
• Major hub for Delta Air Lines; extensive domestic & international network.
• Two parallel runways, massive cargo operations. | | **Los Angeles International** | Los Angeles, CA | LAX | • Second busiest overall; primary gateway to Asia/Pacific.
• Six terminals, three concourses; high volume of international flights.
• Hub for American Airlines and Southwest. | | **Chicago O’Hare International** | Chicago, IL | ORD | • Historically one of the world’s busiest hubs; ~80 M annual passengers pre‑pandemic.
• Four main terminal buildings plus Concourse C.
• Joint hub for United and American airlines. | | **Dallas/Fort Worth International** | Dallas/Fort Worth, TX | DFW | • One of only four U.S. airports serving >70 M travelers annually.
• Dual‑city location serves both metro areas.
• Major hub for American Airlines. | | **Denver International** | Denver, CO | DEN | • Largest single-runway airport worldwide (16 km runway).
• Rapidly growing due to western U.S. expansion.
• Hub for Frontier, United, and Southwest. | | **John F. Kennedy International** | New York City, NY | JFK | • Primary NYC gateway for long-haul carriers (Delta, Korean Air, Emirates).
• Five active terminals; heavy international traffic. | | **San Francisco International** | San Francisco, CA | SFO | • Strong tech‑industry ties; key West Coast hub.
• Known for efficient security lines and green initiatives.
• Hub for United and Alaska Airlines. | | **Seattle/Tacoma International** | Seattle, WA | SEA | • Gateway to Pacific Northwest & Asian markets.
• Home base for Alaska Airlines; strong focus on sustainability. | | **Miami International** | Miami, FL | MIA | • Main entry point from Latin America/Caribbean.
• Growing Hispanic market share; hub for JetBlue and American. | | **Orlando International** | Orlando, FL | ORL | • World's top leisure destination airport (<50 M passengers).
• Serves theme parks, cruise ports, and tourism industry. | | **Phoenix Sky Harbor** | Phoenix, AZ | PHX | • Fastest-growing U.S. airport; hub for American and Southwest.
• High seasonal demand during winter “snowbird” season. | | **George Bush Intercontinental** | Houston, TX | HOU | • Major hub for United; also home to Continental’s legacy fleet.
• Extensive cargo facilities. | | **Charlotte Douglas International** | Charlotte, NC | CLT | • Rising as a secondary hub for American Airlines.
• Strategic East Coast connector. | | **Philadelphia International** | Philadelphia, PA | PHL | • Important Northeast corridor hub; close proximity to Washington DC. | | **Boston Logan International** | Boston, MA | BOS | • Oldest continuously operating airport in the U.S.; vital for Atlantic routes. | ### Why These Airports Matter 1. **Connectivity:** They serve as critical nodes linking domestic regions to global destinations. 2. **Economic Impact:** Each generates billions in local GDP through jobs, tourism, freight, and business travel. 3. **Infrastructure Scale:** Many feature multiple runways, expansive terminals, dedicated cargo centers, and advanced air‑traffic control systems. If you’d like more detail about a particular region, airline hub strategy, or future development plans at any of these airports, just let me know!
